title: Conditions for dispensing into a reusable daily dosage planner
rule_summary: At the patient's or the patient's agent's REQUEST a pharmacy MAY dispense medications in a reusable daily dosage planner provided that: the pharmacy MAY NOT PLACE ANY MEDICATION IN THE PLANNER THAT WAS PREVIOUSLY DISPENSED BY A DIFFERENT PHARMACY; the pharmacy designates a space allowing orderly placement of equipment, materials and medications and preventing cross-contamination; the pharmacy maintains policies and procedures covering cleaning, labeling, dispensing and proper hand hygiene; and the pharmacy cleans and stores planners so as to prevent contamination.
exam_relevance: A common counter request. The decisive limb is provenance: a planner may not be filled with another pharmacy's product, however willing the patient is.

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy regulations

common_confusions: Treating the planner service as a courtesy the pharmacy may run on its own initiative rather than on the patient's or agent's request.
Accepting medication the patient brings from another pharmacy for placement in the planner.
Assuming ordinary labeling duties fall away because the container is a planner.
verification_notes: Read verbatim in the current official publication on 2026-08-20 during Batch 3 tranche B3-F under Issue #91. A fresh independent legal and full-bank realism audit is still required before release.
